short: An idle state the provider puts the machine into by itself.
whyItMatters: Sleep is a policy, not an action. Whether it keeps memory, what counts as activity, and what wakes it decide whether an always-available agent is actually available.

meanings.meaning: A checkpoint of disk and memory, off by default, woken by any request to any URL.
Idle auto-pause: memory kept, wakes on the next API call or URL request; 15–120 minutes by plan.
Hibernate: memory written to disk, ~85 ms wake, disk-only billing. Separate from standby, which keeps RAM.
Idle auto-pause after 30 minutes by default, memory kept; a visit to a public port wakes it, though the API says preview links stay offline.
None. There is no idle timer; the only clock is the lifetime deadline.
Pauses after five idle minutes by default; the next request wakes it, usually within a second.
None. Auto-stop counts from create or resume, not from activity.

checkFor: Ask: what counts as activity, what wakes it, and what does a sleeping hour cost?
